source: Unmodified ac96 generated Phase4Dma.v; preserved hardware default
cause: Phase4Dma.v:175: beat_reg[7'd95:6'(32)*6'd2] has a six-bit lower-bound multiplication, so 64 wraps to zero. The 96-bit slice assigned to a 32-bit result retains lane zero.
related_lane3: Phase4Dma.v:178 similarly narrows 32*3 to 32, retaining lane one.
related_mvout: Phase4Dma.v:390 narrows the second-word slice lower bound to zero; a 192-bit concatenation truncates into 128 bits and temporarily copies word zero into unused lane two. The two-word mask remains 00ff.
migration_contract: BASELINE_TRANSLATED_SLICES=1 is the default and preserves this hardware behavior; explicit 0 follows original Python and is not frozen-hardware equivalent.
reproduction: run_components.sh dma dma-python compares default hardware to frozen HDL and explicit Python mode to the full unmodified-Python trace, including this cycle. dma-python/run.log records 249 cross-mode raw-output differences, not ignored migration-oracle differences.
